# Scope of the Base Problem

The rear axle is an equivalent simply supported, constant-diameter solid circular beam subjected only to the chain-induced transverse point load. The rear axle does not carry wheel-driving torque in this idealization; that torque passes through the sprocket carrier and wheel. The model excludes vehicle/rider weight, tire and road loads, braking, cornering, suspension action, dynamic impact, vibration, fatigue, stress concentrations, threads, shoulders, clamping, detailed bearing contact, and detailed chain/sprocket contact.

# Textbook Connection

The bending-strength portion aligns with Hibbeler, *Mechanics of Materials*, 11th ed., Chapter 6. Problem 6-109 similarly sizes a steel shaft under transverse loading using an allowable bending stress. This problem adds the motorcycle chain-drive load-path step used to generate the transverse axle load.

# Supplemental Assessment Structure

- context interpretation and load path: 20%;
- student idealization and assumptions: 20%;
- chain-force and equilibrium calculations: 20%;
- bending strength and diameter sizing: 30%;
- engineering interpretation and limitations: 10%.
